palm_definition.reason: The +Y broad STL surface faces the positive flexion motion of all four long fingers; -Y is the dorsal side.

gravity_moment_estimate.limitation: COM assumes uniform-density primitive shape volumes and fixed 3/6/6 g masses. Contact proxies are the configured source-mesh points transformed by actual FK, not recorded PhysX contact patch centres. Two ideal point contacts cannot counter a torque about their joining line; finite contact patches may, so this is a mechanism hypothesis rather than a measured stability proof.

candidates.construction: Rigidly rotate the actual settled grasp so its measured tip-spread axis is world -Y; place its orthogonalized mean-blade axis downward at the named table inclination. This changes real physics orientation, not camera.

at_grasp_height.method: Minimum transformed source collision-triangle vertex z; exact for a horizontal infinite plane. Adapter cylinder support function; fixed mounting base excluded.

limitations: The source video is monocular and uncalibrated; its overhead appearance does not determine a unique 3-D palm normal or tool/table inclination. The 30–50 degree range is a requested design target, not a recovered measurement.
No GPU or physics simulation is run by this script. FK reachability and plane clearance do not establish frictional holding stability after gravity reorientation.
The old open060 gravity equilibrium is not valid after a rigid rotation; actual contact forces must be re-established with legal robot actuation and tested after support removal.
Source hand self-intersection distances are unchanged by rigid pose rotation; full arm self-collision and all motion trajectories are not certified here.
Longer blades increase reach/hand clearance but change inertia, gravity torque and opening. They must be rebuilt and retested rather than replaying an old dynamic snapshot as if unchanged.
The original q_reference/closure and shared src files remain unchanged. Each candidate exports actual 18-joint pose, target, wrist pose and three independent dynamic tool-body transforms.
